clue.text: Condition in which none is wanting

definitions.text: Condition in which none is wanting

parts.words: Condition in which none is wanting
parts.note: read 'none is wanting' as 'nobody lacks anything': a state of plenty, of wealth and abundance

explanation.definitionFit: Abundance or wealth is a state where nothing is lacking.

clue.text: Devastation grave as can be

indicators.note: 'as can be' read as 'as it can be made', so the letters are formed into another word

explanation.surface: A scene of ruin as serious as could be imagined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave as can be' reads as 'extremely serious', but 'can be' rearranges GRAVE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravages are destructive effects, the damage left by disaster.

clue.text: Crowd collected to examine the race-track

parts.note: to con is to study or examine closely
a course is a race-track, as in a racecourse

explanation.surface: Spectators gather to inspect the track before a race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people assembled in one place is the old sense of the word.

clue.text: It's simplicity itself

parts.note: 'simplicity itself' usually means very easy, but here means innocent, unworldly simplicity

explanation.definitionFit: Artless innocence is the meaning of simplicity in a person, not ease of a task.

clue.text: Do these birds betray the presence of catfish?

definitions.text: Do these birds betray the presence of catfish?

parts.words: Do these birds betray the presence of catfish?
parts.note: gulls of the coast make a sound like a cat's mew, so a fish that is a cat would also be heard at sea mewing

explanation.walkthrough: A mew is a gull, and also a cat's cry; a cat at sea would make 'sea mews'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mews are gulls, and those over the ocean are named for their cat-like cry.

clue.text: The one we would keep is not a round one

definitions.text: The one we would keep is not a round one

parts.words: The one we would keep is not a round one
parts.note: the shape of the body that dieters want to keep trim, playing on a 'round' number as against a round waistline

explanation.walkthrough: A 'round figure' is a rounded number, but the clue means the body shape: the trim shape we want to keep is not a rounded one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's shape or physique is the sense here, and a round number is the other sense the clue teases.

clue.text: Means of communication between banks

parts.note: the banks are river banks, not financial houses, and the link is a vessel crossing the water

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that carries people across a river links its two shores.

clue.text: New pro's got to be found in Hampshire

indicators.note: a new version of the words is made by arranging their letters afresh

parts.note: the apostrophe-s here counts as a letter S, giving PROS

explanation.surface: A newly signed professional has been placed somewhere in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Gosport is a naval town on the south coast of England in the county of Hampshire; 'New' rearranges PROS and GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a port in that southern English county.

clue.text: The sapper's heart-throb is a throw-back

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE
a pulse is the throb of the heart

explanation.surface: An army engineer's idol turns out to be an evolutionary throwback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-throb' wants to mean an idol, but it is the beat of the heart; 'throw-back' is not a reversion but a driving back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff that drives an attacker back is a repelling, a hurling back.

clue.text: It introduces an air of freshness

definitions.text: It introduces an air of freshness

parts.words: It introduces an air of freshness
parts.note: literally, a device that lets fresh air into a stuffy room, read against 'an air of freshness' as a manner or mood

explanation.definitionFit: A fan or grille that brings outside air into a room is exactly what the clue literally describes.

clue.text: Though chumps they might possibly pass

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the word that follows might be arranged some other way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fools may still scrape through an exam, the setter concedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like the verb of the surface, but 'possibly' makes it anagram fodder, rearranging PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saps and chumps are both informal words for gullible fools.

clue.text: Chaperon a dimwit, but sweet !

parts.note: a gooseberry is an unwanted third person tagging along with a couple, like a chaperon
a fool is a dimwit

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a chaperon for being stupid, yet still finds them charming.
explanation.walkthrough: A gooseberry fool is a British pudding of stewed gooseberries folded into cream or custard; 'sweet' is the British word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is a classic British dessert, and 'sweet' is the British word for a pudding course.

clue.text: Brings to, or conceals from, the public gaze

definitions.text: Brings to, or conceals from, the public gaze

parts.words: Brings to, or conceals from, the public gaze
parts.note: the verb has two opposite senses: showing a film to an audience, and hiding something behind a partition

explanation.definitionFit: Shows a film in a cinema, or shields from view behind a partition: the one verb covers both opposite senses.

clue.text: On reflection, he was lovesick

parts.note: the youth of Greek myth pined for his own image in a pool, so his love fell on a reflection

explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' seems to mean 'thinking it over', but the youth of Greek myth fell in love with his reflection in water.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth wasted away for love of his own image in a pool.

clue.text: Three attendants at the Yard ?

parts.note: a yard is three feet, so three 'attendants' each standing for a foot make up a yard; servants in livery are the real sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, but the yard is the measure of three feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveried servants who wait at doors and table are attendants, and their name splits as 'foot' plus 'men'.

clue.text: Showing signs of attack by a fly-by-night

definitions.text: Showing signs of attack by a fly-by-night

parts.words: Showing signs of attack by a fly-by-night
parts.note: a fly-by-night is usually a dodgy trader, but here a night-flying insect whose larvae chew cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Clothing with holes chewed by insect larvae looks worn and shabby.

clue.text: Where to get stout with plenty of hopping ?

definitions.text: Where to get stout with plenty of hopping ?

parts.words: Where to get stout with plenty of hopping ?
parts.note: stout is a dark beer and hops flavour it; the surface suggests getting fat despite plenty of exercise

explanation.walkthrough: Getting 'stout' through 'hopping' sounds like gaining weight while exercising, but stout is a dark beer brewed with hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where beer such as stout is made, using hops, is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Determine to clear up the mystery again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to solve a mystery is to clear it up

explanation.surface: A detective decides to reopen the case and crack it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to decide firmly, which is to make up one's mind.

clue.text: A good blubber would do them a lot of good

definitions.text: A good blubber would do them a lot of good

parts.words: A good blubber would do them a lot of good
parts.note: a 'good blubber' sounds like a long cry, but blubber is whale fat, which hunters prize

explanation.definitionFit: Ships and crews hunting whales profited from the fat of a catch.

clue.text: Tar must be re-applied in a layer

indicators.note: the letters are applied again in a fresh order, which signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Road tar has to be laid again, spread in a fresh coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-applied' rearranges TAR and MUST. The OCR text had 'Car'; the printed page reads 'Tar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a single bed or level of rock or other material.

clue.text: A miner's involved in this study group

indicators.note: 'involved' in the sense of twisted or entangled says the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the apostrophe-s counts as a letter S, giving MINERS

explanation.surface: A coal miner takes part in a discussion class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A MINERS; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class meeting for discussion and study.

clue.text: Platform, not 21 ac's, but an odd sort, unusual

indicators.note: 'odd' as in strange says the word next to it is put into a strange order

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or unusual

explanation.surface: A stage not of the railway kind, but a peculiar, unusual one.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is STATIONMASTERS, whose platforms are at railway stations; this one is a speaker's platform. 'odd' rearranges SORT to ROST.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand for a speaker or conductor is a platform of another kind.

clue.text: In the south of France a blow to a poet

definitions.text: In the south of France a blow
definitions.meaning: a cold north wind that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France
Frédéric ... was a Provençal poet who won the Nobel Prize

explanation.surface: A Provençal poet suffers a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a strong Provençal wind and that of a Nobel-winning poet from Provence.

clue.text: They have positions lined up for them

definitions.text: They have positions lined up for them

parts.words: They have positions lined up for them
parts.note: 'positions lined up' reads as jobs waiting, but means railway stations along a line, each run by these officials

explanation.definitionFit: Each runs a railway stop, a position on the line, so their posts are literally lined up.

clue.text: This is also the answer

parts.note: the thing you are reading points to the solution, and here it names itself

explanation.definitionFit: A crossword hint leads to the solution, and the word for such a hint is itself the solution here.

clue.text: He doesn't object to his letters being read

definitions.text: He doesn't object to his letters being read

parts.words: He doesn't object to his letters being read
parts.note: his 'letters' are not correspondence but the painted lettering on shop fronts, made to be read by everyone

explanation.definitionFit: A painter of shop and inn boards produces lettering meant to be read publicly.

clue.text: A perceptive quintette

parts.note: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch make a group of five faculties of perception

explanation.definitionFit: Sight, hearing, touch, taste and smell are the five faculties of perception.

clue.text: Bad type is told he won't get paid

definitions.text: Bad type is told he won't get paid

parts.words: Bad type is told he won't get paid
parts.note: the lawbreaker learns the old saying that crime does not pay

explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the proverb 'crime doesn't pay': the wrongdoer is told it will bring no reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker is a bad type, and the proverb says his line of work earns nothing.
